title: SOC 2
summary: SOC 2 is an attestation report issued under the AICPA Trust Services Criteria that describes how a service organisation designs and, in a Type 2 report, operates controls relevant to the security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality and privacy of customer data. It is not a certification and there is no pass or fail: an independent CPA firm expresses an opinion on whether management's description of its system is accurate and whether the selected controls operated effectively over a defined review period. Two report types exist. A Type 1 report speaks to control design at a single point in time and is frequently used to unblock early enterprise deals; a Type 2 report covers design and operating effectiveness across a window, commonly three to twelve months, and is what mature buyers demand. The Common Criteria, organised around control environment, communication and information, risk assessment, monitoring activities and control activities, map closely to how engineering teams already work, which is why SOC 2 readiness often reduces to formalising change management, access review, vulnerability management, incident response and vendor risk processes that already exist informally. For practitioners the practical work is defining the system boundary, producing a control matrix with named owners, gathering evidence on a schedule rather than in a panic, and being precise in the description of the system. Bridge letters and complementary user entity controls matter because responsibilities split between the provider and the customer.
objectives: You will be able to distinguish a SOC 2 Type 1 design opinion from a Type 2 operating effectiveness opinion and explain the review period.
You will be able to define a service organisation's system boundary and the infrastructure, software, people and procedures inside it.
You will be able to map the Trust Services Criteria to existing engineering controls and assign named control owners.
You will be able to design an evidence cadence that keeps access reviews, change tickets and monitoring artefacts audit-ready year round.
You will be able to interpret a bridge letter and complementary user entity controls in a vendor due diligence review.
You will be able to spot the difference between a control that is documented and a control that actually operated.
